q: A user logs into a portal using a password and a code from a physical hardware token. Which authentication factor categories are being used?
opts: Something you know and something you are
Something you have and somewhere you are
Something you know and something you have
Something you are and something you have
exp: A password represents "something you know," and a physical token represents "something you have."

wrongFeedback.0: A hardware token is a possession factor ("have"), not a biometric trait ("are").
wrongFeedback.1: A password is a knowledge factor ("know"), not a geographic attribute ("somewhere").
wrongFeedback.3: Neither authentication credential relies on biometric characteristics ("something you are").

q: An organization protects its web portal using a password and a time-based one-time passcode (TOTP). An employee enters both credentials into a lookalike phishing site, and an attacker immediately logs into the victim's legitimate account. Which factor explains why multi-factor authentication failed to prevent this breach?
opts: The authentication mechanism relied on static session cookies that never expire.
The one-time code was intercepted and relayed to the service before expiration.
The mobile application failed to implement secure out-of-band communication.
The encryption keys used to generate the temporary passcodes were compromised.
exp: Standard TOTP passcodes lack cryptographic binding to the website's domain origin. An adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) reverse proxy can capture the submitted code and submit it to the genuine portal before the 30-second window lapses.

wrongFeedback.0: Session cookie expiration settings govern persistent access after authentication occurs, but they do not cause or explain the initial credential bypass during the login handshake.
wrongFeedback.2: TOTP generation is computed locally using a shared secret and current time; it does not require an out-of-band transmission channel (unlike SMS or push alerts).
wrongFeedback.3: The attacker did not reverse-engineer or steal the underlying HMAC secret key stored on the server; they simply harvested and forwarded the user-supplied output in real time.
